title.narrative: A transdisciplinary approach towards restoring selected South African peatland ecosystems and their catchments

description.narrative: Note: Disbursement data provided is cumulative and covers disbursement made by the project Agency.

There are marked difference between women and men in the use and governance of natural ecosystems, particularly in rural areas under traditional and customary land tenure systems. Women are typically the primary users of natural resources, and often the most affected by environmental degradation. Women have a key role to play in environmental management and decision-making, yet they are often largely excluded. The lack of participation by women in governance and decision-making systems weakens resource use and ecosystem management. This also has negative consequences for the equitable participation of women in the restoration economy. The restoration economy refers specifically to economic activity relating to ecological restoration initiatives, which contribute to national economic growth as well as generate a range of benefits including creating jobs, developing skills and connecting people to their natural environments. Women must have opportunities to engage equitably in all dimensions of the restoration economy, from decision-making and process development to implementation, monitoring and evaluation. Empowering women’s participation in the restoration economy requires a multidimensional approach in order to address social, economic and systemic barriers. The project has potential to support South Africa’s progress towards key SGDs through the following pathways, with global benefits: • Improving household water security (SDG 3 and 6) through peatland restoration and associated links to the allocation and management of water rights • Promoting gender equity (SDG 5 and 10) through strengthening capacity and participation of women, men, youth and marginalized and vulnerable people in decision-making and equitable benefit sharing opportunities. • Addressing unemployment and poverty (SDG 8) through creating green jobs and increasing opportunities in the green economy through creating financing and investment for peatland restoration. To upscale peatland restoration efforts, the project intends to establish an enabling environment conducive to medium to long-term investment opportunities in peatland and catchment restoration and management, emphasizing benefits to communities. This will entail the creation of technical assistance facilities to facilitate blended finance investment for South Africa's peatlands, as well as the identification and preparation of investment opportunities. To support the upscaling of peatland restoration and management, evidence of the benefits associated with these practices will be generated through the long-term monitoring of biophysical components at each pilot site. In addition, the South African peatland database will be updated, and a national peatland map produced for South Africa. From a local perspective, restoring peatlands will contribute towards enhanced water availability through the ability of intact peatlands to store water and regulate flow. Intact peatlands are also able to mitigate against flood events through reducing stormwater flows. This will reduce downstream damage to infrastructure following storm events. Intact peatlands will also contribute towards local biodiversity through providing habitat connectivity, sources of water, stopover sites for birds, and breeding areas for many species. Other local benefits include the provision of jobs through the management and implementation phase of this project as well as the postgraduate students performing research on the study sites. All job and student appointments will follow strict gender equity principles. Preventing peatlands from burning and needing to be extinguished, and preventing peatlands from eroding to and downstream flooding will avoid unnecessary costs related to disaster risk management.
To restore the ecosystem functions of three South African peatland systems and their catchments for the provision of benefits to communities while contributing to global environmental goals
